source.name: sp_SharedTempReport

result.generatedDdl:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.sp_SharedTempReport()
RETURNS TABLE (
    OrderDate DATE,
    TotalOrders INT,
    TotalRevenue DECIMAL(12,2)
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    -- PostgreSQL uses local temporary tables instead of global temp tables
    -- The temp table will be automatically dropped at the end of the session
    CREATE TEMP TABLE IF NOT EXISTS temp_global_order_summary (
        OrderDate DATE,
        TotalOrders INT,
        TotalRevenue DECIMAL(12,2)
    ) ON COMMIT DROP;

    -- Clear any existing data if table already exists
    DELETE FROM temp_global_order_summary;

    INSERT INTO temp_global_order_summary
    SELECT
        CAST(OrderDate AS DATE),
        COUNT(*)::INT,
        SUM(TotalAmount)
    FROM dbo.Orders
    GROUP BY CAST(OrderDate AS DATE);

    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT 
        t.OrderDate,
        t.TotalOrders,
        t.TotalRevenue
    FROM temp_global_order_summary t
    ORDER BY t.OrderDate DESC;

    -- Temp table will be dropped automatically due to ON COMMIT DROP
END;
$$;
assumptions: The global temporary table ##GlobalOrderSummary is converted to a local temporary table with ON COMMIT DROP, as PostgreSQL does not have true global temporary tables
The procedure returns a result set, so it is converted to a FUNCTION returning TABLE
The dbo.Orders table exists in PostgreSQL with the same schema (OrderDate and TotalAmount columns)
SET NOCOUNT ON is omitted as PostgreSQL functions don't send row count messages by default
The temporary table is created with IF NOT EXISTS and cleared before use to handle potential multiple calls within the same transaction
Standard type mappings applied: DATE→DATE, INT→INT, DECIMAL(12,2)→DECIMAL(12,2)

reviewFlags.reason: Global temporary tables (##) in SQL Server are visible across sessions, but PostgreSQL temporary tables are session-scoped only. If cross-session visibility is required, consider using a permanent application table with session tracking or advisory locks.
reviewFlags.codeSection: CREATE TEMP TABLE IF NOT EXISTS temp_global_order_summary ... ON COMMIT DROP

reviewFlags.reason: Verify that the dbo.Orders table exists in PostgreSQL with the correct schema, including OrderDate and TotalAmount columns with compatible data types.

The temporary table will be dropped at transaction commit. If the function is called multiple times within the same transaction, this behavior may differ from SQL Server's global temp table semantics. Consider using ON COMMIT DELETE ROWS instead if persistence within transaction is needed.

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server's ##GlobalOrderSummary is a global temporary table visible across all sessions until explicitly dropped or server restart. PostgreSQL temporary tables are session-scoped and not visible to other sessions. This changes the sharing semantics significantly.

The ON COMMIT DROP clause causes the temp table to be dropped at the end of each transaction. If autocommit is on, this happens immediately after the function completes. This may differ from SQL Server behavior where the global temp table persists until explicitly dropped.

Converted from a procedure with SELECT output to a function returning TABLE. Calling code must be updated to SELECT FROM the function: SELECT * FROM dbo.sp_SharedTempReport() instead of EXEC dbo.sp_SharedTempReport.
Added explicit ::INT cast for COUNT(*) to ensure type compatibility with the return table definition, though this is typically implicit in PostgreSQL.
